newsitem.title: HUNGARY: NEW GROUP CLAIMS RESPONSIBILITY FOR BUDAPEST BOMBS.
newsitem.headline: NEW GROUP CLAIMS RESPONSIBILITY FOR BUDAPEST BOMBS.

text.p: A organisation calling itself the Hungarian Will of Gods (IMA) claimed responsibility on Friday for two recent bomb blasts in Budapest near Europe's largest synanogue.
The Hungarian daily Mai Nap said a man called the paper by telephone on Thursday, saying the previously unheard of organisation had planted a bomb in a dustbin near the Dohany utca synagogue.
The Hungarian acronym of the organisation "IMA" means prayer.

The person, who declined to name himself, disclosed details about the mechanism of the bomb, which exploded on Wednesday night, and another one, which blew up on August 25 on a bench in Klauzal Square, about 100 meters from a kosher restaurant in the heart of the former Jewish ghetto.
The bombs did not hurt anyone, but heightened concern in Hungary's Jewish community that a pattern may be developing.
Laszlo Garamvolgyi, spokesman of the police told Reuters the police are searching intensively for those who planted the bombs as well as the person who telephoned to Mai Nap.
"It is not sure yet that (the telephone caller) was the culprit," Garamvolgyi said, adding he did not believe the caller was a member of a terrorist organisation.
